title: Effectual Calling and Regeneration
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro
series: Soteriology: The Westminster Confession of Faith

outline.title: The Nature of the Westminster Confession
subpoints: The Confession is a subordinate standard, not the Word of God
It serves as a systematic summary of biblical doctrine

outline.title: Effectual Calling vs. General Call
subpoints: The general call invites all to repent and believe (e.g., Isaiah 55:1)
The effectual call is a special grace given only to the elect
The effectual call is irresistible and results in salvation

outline.title: The Means of Calling
subpoints: The call comes through the proclamation of the Word
Faith comes from hearing the gospel
The Holy Spirit works through the preached Word to give life

outline.title: Regeneration: The Change of Nature
subpoints: Regeneration is synonymous with being born again
God changes the sinner's nature before they come to faith
Believers come willingly because their hearts have been renewed

summary:
This session continues the study of soteriology through the Westminster Confession of Faith, focusing on Chapter 10: Effectual Calling. The speaker clarifies the church's view of the Confession as a subordinate standard—a helpful, systematic summary of Scripture that is distinct from the inspired Word of God. The primary focus is distinguishing between the general call of the gospel, which is offered freely to all, and the effectual call, which is a special grace extended only to the elect. This effectual call is described as irresistible, meaning it successfully brings the recipient to faith and salvation, as illustrated by the chain of redemption in Romans 8:30.

The sermon emphasizes that the means of this calling is the proclamation of the Word. Using the parable of the dry bones in Ezekiel 37, the speaker illustrates how the Holy Spirit uses the preached gospel to give life to those who are spiritually dead. The text highlights that while the general call invites all to come, the effectual call ensures that those predestined for life will indeed come to Christ.

Finally, the doctrine of regeneration is introduced as another perspective on effectual calling. Regeneration, or being born again, is the internal work of God that changes a person's nature. Rather than forcing individuals to believe against their will, God renews their hearts and wills, enabling them to respond to the gospel freely and willingly. This transformation is evidenced in Ephesians 2, where believers are described as being made alive by grace before they exercise faith.
